Report Description
****WEB REPORT**** RECEIVED A CALL THIS AFTERNOON INDICATING THAT WE HAD A CONSTRUCTION ACCIDENT ON OUR STANDING BEAR BRIDGE ER (FEDERAL EMERGENCY RELIEF PROGRAM) BANK ARMOR PROJECT. FROM THE LIMITED INFORMATION THAT I HAVE, IT SOUNDS AS IF TRACK TYPE EXCAVATOR FELL INTO THE WATER AS THEY WERE PLACING RIP-RAP MATERIAL AND WAS ALMOST COMPLETELY SUBMERGED (THE OPERATOR WAS ABLE TO GET OUT OF THE MACHINE SAFELY). THERE WAS AN ATTEMPT TO RECOVER THE MACHINE FROM THE ROADWAY BUT THE CABLES USED IN THAT ATTEMPT SNAPPED AND THE EXCAVATOR IS NOW TOTALLY SUBMERGED. CURRENTLY, THE CONTRACTOR IS PLACING RIP-RAP MATERIAL IN THE WATER TO BUILD A WORK PLATFORM WHERE THEY CAN SAFELY ATTEMPT TO REMOVE THE MACHINE. WE WILL HAVE THE CONTRACTOR REMOVE THE RIP-RAP MATERIAL UPON RECOVERY OF THE MACHINE. THE RIP-RAP MAY BE IN PLACE THREE (3) WEEKS OR LONGER DEPENDING ON THE DIFFICULTY OF REMOVING THE MACHINE AND FUTURE ICE CONDITIONS THAT MAY HAMPER THE REMOVAL OF THE RIP-RAP PLACED FOR THE RECOVERY WORK PAD. NO OBVIOUS FUEL OR OIL PRODUCT DISCHARGE HAS BEEN OBSERVED AT THAT TIME. SINCE THEN A SECOND ATTEMPT TO REMOVE THE MACHINE WAS MADE AND I UNDERSTAND AN OIL FILTER WAS DAMAGED IN THAT ATTEMPT AND A SMALL AMOUNT OF OIL HAS BEEN RELEASED. I UNDERSTAND THAT THE OIL MATERIAL IS BASICALLY FROZEN IN PLACE WITH THE ICE AROUND THE MACHINE AT THE RELEASE SITE. THIS INCIDENT IS LOCATED IN A BACKWATER AREA AWAY FROM THE FLOWING CHANNEL ARE OF THE MISSOURI RIVER
